resources.title: CyberChef: how recipes work and worked examples
resources.learn: Learn the input/recipe/output workflow; follow Base64, hexdump, compression and nested-encoding examples. Start here before trying random operations.
resources.offline: Save the README and prepare a working local CyberChef build before departure; a bookmark alone is not an offline copy. Test it with networking disabled.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read upstream README sections on capabilities, local execution and recipe examples through Exa. No local build tested.

resources.title: Cryptography Lab 5: Cooking with the Cyberchef
resources.learn: A short visual introduction to reversible recipes, Base64, octal and a multi-step obfuscation exercise. The simple typed-text example can be recreated without the course.
resources.offline: Use the platform’s permitted offline option before flying. Later lab material references a course-provided obfuscated-code file; that file was not obtained.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Inspected creator video metadata and transcript covering the interface and layered encoding through Exa; not watched. Listed runtime is 7:17; study estimate includes pausing.

resources.title: CTFlearn: RSA Beginner
resources.learn: Follow n, e and c through factorization, totient, modular inverse and Python byte conversion. This explains the prerequisites behind automated RSA tools.
resources.offline: Save using a permitted video offline option. The demo uses online SageCell: replace that step with an already-tested local Sage installation for public toy inputs; do not copy the online submission workflow with event challenge material.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Inspected creator metadata and full retrieved transcript through Exa; not watched. Listed runtime is 5:44. This demonstrates textbook weak RSA, not general RSA breaking.

resources.title: RsaCtfTool: usage and attack prerequisites
resources.learn: Learn public-key inspection, selected attacks and decryption inputs; distinguish close-prime, small-exponent and shared-factor situations from unfactorable keys.
resources.offline: Save README and help output. Prepare dependencies beforehand; Sage is optional for some attacks but needed for others. Avoid network-backed attacks such as FactorDB offline.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read upstream README usage, requirements, examples and attack table through Exa. Current README can differ from the organiser’s unspecified latest revision; commands not executed.

resources.title: SageMath tutorial: number theory
resources.learn: Work through modular rings, gcd, factor, inverse_mod and CRT examples. Compare Sage syntax with the provided Python equivalents.
resources.offline: Save this chapter and test local Sage first. The workbook records no Sage installation information; ordinary Python alone does not provide sage.all.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read official number-theory tutorial examples through Exa; examples not executed.

resources.title: hashcat: attack modes, options and status output
resources.learn: Focus on choosing hash type versus attack mode, supplying a wordlist or mask, and interpreting progress, rejected candidates and recovered hashes. Consult local help before copying flags.
resources.offline: Save the page and prepare a tiny self-created hash/wordlist exercise before flying. Device backend and drivers must already work; long GPU searches are poor battery exercises.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Fetched official wiki through Exa and inspected version, status output and options introduction. Page states 7.1.2, matching the workbook; no cracking or hardware check run.

resources.title: John the Ripper: usage examples
resources.learn: Learn single mode, wordlist rules and --show; understand why selecting candidates matters more than immediately running exhaustive incremental search.
resources.offline: Save the examples and prepare a tiny synthetic hash file and wordlist. The page teaches general John behavior; Jumbo-specific formats and extractors need the installed build’s help.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read upstream examples through Exa, including default mode order, wordlist rules and pot-file display. No extraction or cracking run.

resources.title: bkcrack: official encrypted-ZIP tutorial
resources.learn: Inspect ZipCrypto versus compression, identify known plaintext, recover internal keys and decrypt the provided public example. Keys can recover data without first recovering the original password.
resources.offline: Before departure, obtain the public repository’s example/secrets.zip and tutorial plus a working bkcrack binary; test on your own device. Nothing downloaded here. Targets ZipCrypto, not AES ZIP; at least 12 known bytes are needed, including 8 contiguous bytes.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read upstream tutorial and repository README through Exa; confirmed bundled public example and plaintext requirements. Tutorial follows current master and may differ from workbook 1.8.1; exercise not run.

resources.title: crypto-attacks: requirements and worked Boneh–Durfee example
resources.learn: See how an attack implementation consumes mathematical parameters and how its test data provides a reproducible starting point. Advanced follow-up after basic RSA and Sage, not a universal one-command solver.
resources.offline: Save the repository and its test data beforehand if pursuing this optional exercise. README requires Sage with Python 3.9 and PyCryptodome; test compatibility with the actual environment before travel.
resources.verification: 2026-10-22: Read upstream README requirements and worked example through Exa. Repository tests and example were not run; installed revision is not captured in the workbook.
